title: Finite assembly, source-basis cost reduction, and E8 verification
body:
This PR contributes constructive finite assembly parameters, a reusable reduction in the bit supplier’s finite overcharge, a parent-contract guard for the hosted bit audit, and faster source-equivalent hashing and scalar replay in the E8 emitter. Earlier bank optimization and verification tools are retained.

Fixed backoffs and a fixed bootstrap depth leave an avoidable gap below the balanced assembly's supplied-cap ceiling. This PR adds a constructive theorem and exact verifier that select finite parameters for **every rational target below `min(b,c)/(1+min(b,c))`**, given admitted bit and complex caps and the retained conditional interfaces.

The [new package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier) chooses strictly positive backoffs, a finite number of bootstrap steps and explicit integer cutoffs. The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/finite-assembly-frontier/PROOF.md) establishes termination and all 47 retained strict outer inequalities. It also proves maximality on a supplied rational grid, relative to these caps and this assembly family. The ceiling itself is not attained.

### Reusable source-basis finite-cost reduction

The [source-basis package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order) now provides a guarded postprocessor that derives the copied forms from the actual input word. It preserves their order, their literal inverse, the set of source rows entering the full frame, and the surrounding construction. A separate postprocessing stage lets it compose with frozen reset/kernel selections without changing their original hashes or receipts.

| Pinned construction | Complete finite coefficient | Two-level coefficient | Extra local additions |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR433 R758 | 223 to 192 bits | 483 to 420 bits | 32 |
| PR438 R747 after resets/kernel | 226 to 193 bits | 488 to 423 bits | 32 |

The added operations are fully charged. The lower cancellation-free prefix dominates that added cost. **Both supplier caps and the multiplication exponent stay unchanged.** This improves a rigorous finite overcharge; it makes no practical runtime or current numerical lead claim. It is not guaranteed to improve every word.

The PR433 five-stage changed-bit run is retained. On [PR438](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/438), pinned at `e3b56de7869f6af88d48ac0ab1d7959c4c9e6176`, all nine stages passed in one 18.49-second run: original construction/reset/kernel checks, the separate basis stage, and unchanged exporter/global/audit/price/combined checks. The new word restores all 987 local and 7,683 global columns, with eight bank controls, four outer controls and all 47 strict inequalities passing. Its κ remains `45340333148791/40000000000000000`.

The candidate has a fresh complete invoice. The baseline cost is reconstructed from its literally replayed word and the unchanged verified geometry/schedule; its full global pipeline was not rerun. Eleven unchanged outputs from the independently completed PR433 complex component are explicitly reused, with source, canonical-word and recipe bindings. No new complex or phase execution is claimed.

The [proof](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/blob/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-bit-basis-order/PROOF.md), source bindings, exact executed adapters, original/new words, receipts and stage logs are retained. The self-contained audit independently checks both constructions' literal orientations, copied forms, omission controls, prefix growth and complete invoices. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 75-input package; manifest is `3df3113896b1130f2770f26da08ec7f4b812e822d568cce69b0f75ba7eb2cd17`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/verify.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/test_postprocess.py
python3 -B research/e8-bit-basis-order/postprocess.py original.json candidate.json
```

Three focused test contracts cover both exact reconstructions, input preservation and idempotence, unsafe basis interfaces, and CLI overwrite protection. The output is a candidate: each new word still needs its supplier's complete admission checks. The postprocessor and offline audit are portable. The retained PR438 adapter records the exact executed temporary paths; it is evidence, not a portable CLI. The existing PR433 full replay wrapper has input-only validation, with its original completed scientific run retained separately.

### Preserve the inherited contract in the hosted bit audit

The original [PR442](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/442) generator preserves its parent scalar schedule, but its independent bit hosting audit does not enforce that preservation. On the authentic published hosted template, deleting the terminal exchange or zeroing a bridge coefficient is accepted with an unchanged paid profile, although literal F2 replay finds eight or three wrong scalar columns, respectively. **These are deliberately mutated regressions; the actual published construction is not alleged invalid.**

The new [guard and integration patch](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-hosted-bit-contract) enforce the parent schedule, scalar columns, levels, invocation headers and inherited template fields. Only the bit generator's documented hosting changes are permitted. The original ownership/profile audit remains required; the complex side has different permitted edits and is outside this guard's scope.

The positive fixture exactly matches PR442 commit `4e16d001d505d4f21dd2bcfc44591f9be4c279bd` and template payload `dd7833dcaff8c84b258847f4c4d65b6402c702700ae37d2c464083ee37b24126`. One seven-stage, 4.43-second bit-only reconstruction reused an exact completed reset word, then ran the original kernel, exporter, source-span check, global emitter, parent audit, hosted generator and regression probe. The parent kernel's three controls and audit's eight controls passed. No complex, phase, pricing or assembly replay was performed; no new bound is claimed.

Four focused test contracts cover the authentic positive, the two original-audit false negatives with independent scalar replay, sign/level/header/index/field mutations, and a matching invalid parent/child pair. The offline verifier checks the source/Git bindings, payload hashes, logs and receipts, and executes the exact two-line integration patch in memory. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 38-input package, manifest `f15db9c1ae361b6d0b1f230a23cf6da02add4ea70c1e5907c80d42d9301eac57`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-hosted-bit-contract/verify.py
```

### Byte-identical emitter digest caching

The [emitter cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/2c47125cbb0619dc63ccdf64c9c583f064240aeb/research/e8-emitter-digest-cache) removes repeated JSON serialization from the pinned [PR447 emitter](https://github.com/rohanarun/integer-mult-bounds/blob/43e5aa3a2fb6701b1facf542f7f3dee0fbb33c3e/research/e8-eleven-hosting-selected/code/emit.py). It encodes each immutable instruction tail once per orientation and each owner descriptor once per call. A minimal integration patch preserves event order, paid-rank increments, ownership assertions and all other emitter checks.

Across **2,742,552 records and 144 calls** from completed PR438 and authentic PR442 bit workloads, every record byte, independent complete digest, event count and local paid profile matches. The exact source-extracted hashing loop measured a median **3.206 seconds before and 0.587 seconds after**, a **5.47x hashing-loop speedup**. Three alternating trials include cache construction. Template loading, geometry checks, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8, not a whole-emitter speedup or a fresh PR447 scientific replay.

The byte-preservation proof covers the pinned event schema and immutable inputs. The portable offline verifier checks source/Git/fixture/receipt bindings, exact patch scope, every record, and two focused contracts for JSON escaping, large integer tails, fresh per-call owners and malformed inputs. The recorded adapter and original notices are retained. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes. Package manifest: `f45b0dd2c710838f4e5df1c1450c444a7235720b286e89ba946612081c5f847f`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-emitter-digest-cache/verify.py
```

Default verification does not rerun the benchmark. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted loop on another machine.

### Stage-local address caching for scalar replay

The [scalar address-cache package](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/e500c9c4217483de882cf06e6e80b25b70ea1ca5/research/e8-scalar-address-cache) removes repeated local-to-global mapper calls from the same pinned PR447 emitter. Its two-line integration patch constructs one address table per local stage, including the private scratch index. All original scalar, dirty-helper, private restoration, stage, terminal and integer bridge controls remain intact.

On two retained local-word workloads, three alternating trials measured **1.736x and 1.730x faster scalar replay**, respectively: **35.984 to 20.728 ms** for the completed PR438 word and **35.774 to 20.676 ms** for the authentic PR442 template's local word. Timing includes address-table construction and the complete extracted scalar-replay section through its 24 bridge-omission controls. Template loading, AST extraction, geometry, hosting, compression and other supplier work are excluded. This is a microbenchmark on macOS arm64/Python 3.14.8; the cache adds O(LOCAL) storage per active stage.

Both versions independently return identical complete values, levels, schedules, stage receipts and controls. The contract checks **648,692 operand mappings**, both reflections, all **11 stages and 9,417 basis columns per workload**, private restoration and all 24 bridge controls. The retained PR438/PR442 local words are used with the pinned eleven-stage recipe; this is not a fresh full PR447 admission. No mathematical bound or finite coefficient changes, and no whole-emitter speedup is claimed.

The proof states the valid-index and stage-immutability preconditions. The portable offline verifier binds original source/Git/license/fixture/receipt bytes, checks exact patch scope, repeats the complete equivalence contract, and covers address-block boundaries, per-stage cache freshness, invalid operands and omission of the private endpoint. It also reproduces identical combined source when the address and digest patches are applied in either order. Their separately measured speedups must not be multiplied into an overall speedup. Ody independently reviewed the frozen 32-input package, manifest `643da0bb1ae5f1453f0c31574ac78b08ec7c3f9836126a8c4dbdedeef8cf61af`.

```sh
python3 -B research/e8-scalar-address-cache/verify.py
```

Default validation does not repeat timing or any supplier wrapper. Add `--benchmark` to measure the extracted section on another machine.

### Finite-assembly worked example

Using the unchanged suppliers from [PR433](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/433), pinned to `6d9244518175caf9e0089f92486959bc2c317273`, the greatest admitted point on a `10^-27` grid is

```
kappa = 280216238064569651155257 / 250000000000000000000000000
      = 0.001120864952258278604621028
```

This is strictly above that source's `0.001120864952258278`, by approximately **6.04621e-19**. The numerical gain is tiny. The reusable parameter theorem and verifier are the main contribution; no new supplier word, practical speedup or global optimality is claimed. Later supplier contributions, including [PR434](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/434), report higher bounds. This pinned example is not a claim to the current numerical lead; the parameter theorem applies to future admitted caps as well.

One clean default replay of the pinned supplier package passed all 13 stages in 6.19 seconds. It regenerated both changed programs, their scalar and ownership checks, moments and finite invoices; the original verifier reused its source-bound Gaussian phase evidence. We did not rerun every Gaussian pair. Actual receipts and all stage logs are retained. The new verifier independently reproduces the original assembly, recomputes both supplier moments and the selected seed with two rational engines, checks the actual 483-bit two-level coefficient against its 512-bit charge, and verifies nine finite bootstrap steps and all 47 strict inequalities. The next grid point, zero eta, zero beta and unit beta are rejected.

Five focused tests cover both binding components, equal caps, 48 cap/target regimes, exact grid endpoints, 100-digit grids, zero-step cases and invalid premises. Ody independently reviewed the proof and code and reran the complete package successfully. All 50 package inputs match manifest `876412045fcd74e87bba4f02704eb312fad77e565e73eecb1c4849e1df92ff8d`. The CLI also exports witnesses whose rational numerators exceed Python’s default decimal conversion limit; an end-to-end 100-digit-grid regression covers this. An integration test connects this offline verifier to the existing Python 3.11/3.13/3.14 test matrix, without a new workflow or executor.

```sh
python3 -B research/finite-assembly-frontier/verify.py
```

Add `--output /absolute/path/to/new-result.json` to retain every exact parameter, cutoff and margin. Python 3.11+ and the standard library suffice.

**Current signed, GitHub-verified head:** [`a65780b`](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/commit/a65780b0d5664c33da16e704de4d6f228a7b816b). All 60 jobs across five triggered workflows pass on this exact head: [research/formal, 52 jobs](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135907), [terminal elimination](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203136057), [recycled registers](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135954), [early reset/kernel composition](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135904), and [graded box convolution](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/38203135946). The upstream merge preserves all mathematical results and PR contributions; its follow-up refreshes only the mixed-point audit source hash after upstream’s rational-frame optimization. All 11 focused mixed-point/rational-frame tests also pass locally. No new mathematical bound is claimed.

### Earlier contributions retained

- [Exact bank optimizer](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-exact-bank-optimizer): necessary-and-sufficient packing conditions, optimal patterns and minimum replication for the width-73 rank family. An independent exhaustive oracle checks 16,875 inventories.
- [Chart-sensitive dirty-endpoint audit](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-dirty-chart-audit): exact all-address Gaussian checking, including a counterexample invisible at address zero and an admitted positive control. Six focused regressions pass. Its obstruction is scoped to the stated independent-bank interface.
- [E8 retimed component verification](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/e8-retimed-component-verification): retained emitter, phase, lifetime and finite-accounting evidence for the pinned PR384 complex component.
- [Weighted donor-rank matching](https://github.com/lydakis/integer-mult-bounds/tree/a8be7ab24a5b0da1c7fdaa58e6656ebc774121cf/research/gen5b-weighted-matching): the earlier reproducible construction reused by later contributions. Its historical conditional bound is `0.000751075693834608`; later suppliers improve it.

The supplier compiler, compressed-window, arbitrary dirty-bank, restored-work, fixed-tape/common-grid, precision and analytic interfaces remain assumptions. This is a conditional finite construction, with no unconditional multiplication theorem or new Lean proof.

New parameter selection, source-basis ordering and postprocessor, hosted-bit parent-contract guard, emitter digest and scalar address caching, proofs, tests and evidence integration: George Lydakis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance, including Ody's independent review. PR447's emitter retains rohanarun's original notices and Codex-assistance attribution. PR442's hosting construction and original audit retain the DaysSky package's original notices and Claude-assistance attribution. PR438's reset/kernel construction remains credited to rohanarun; the kernel method and exact engine retain Chafik Boukhalfa's (chafreaky) attribution. PR433's construction remains credited to icekylinx with OpenAI Codex; its upstream lineage includes Zhihao Chen, ai-nanachi, Dylan Crow, Jacob Sussman and the retained contributors. The unchanged outer engine retains its eumemic/Anthropic Claude, icekylinx, Zhihao Chen and RaD/hipotures credits. Original notices, licenses, source pins and earlier package attribution are preserved.
